analysis.title: Monthly Gold Compass, November 2026
key_insights: Gold is down 10.2% YTD in USD through 10/31/2026 after gains of 27.2% in 2024 and 64.4% in 2025. It trades at USD 3,875, versus an all-time high implied at roughly 5,595 on the long-run chart.
Gold's 2026 YTD decline is broad across currencies: AUD -14.8%, CNY -14.5%, GBP -9.6%, JPY -9.7%, CHF -6.5%, EUR -5.5%, INR -5.2%. The average across the nine major currencies is -9.4%.
Gold in USD fell 6.76% in October 2026 and 6.57% in September. Silver fell 18.71% in October and is down 31.1% YTD in USD, at 49.10.
Miners fell harder than bullion in October: HUI -12.15%, GDX -12.20%, GDXJ -16.66%, SIL -17.16%, SILJ -17.56%. GDX is at 77.1 and HUI at 649.7.

Gold-GDX correlation is 0.94 over 15 days and 0.90 over 90 days. Gold's correlation with DXY is -0.42 over 90 days and with the S&P 500 is 0.41 over 90 days. Gold's correlation with WTI is negative at all windows shown.
Gold is down about 27% from its all-time high in USD. Gold in KRW is 33.3% below its ATH, in NOK 31.2%, in AUD 28.2%, and in PLN 20.8%.
Gold's seasonality is positive in November (geometric mean +0.9%) and December (+1.1%).

Inflation has re-accelerated. US CPI was 3.74% y/y in Sep-26 (peak 4.25% in May-26), core CPI 2.57%, PCE 3.65%, core PCE 3.12%, PPI 6.35%, and import prices 8.10%. Euro area HICP was 3.78%, Italy 4.17%, Australia 4.30%.
Rates: the US 2Y yield is 4.58% and the US 10Y is 4.93%. The effective fed funds rate was 3.88% on 10/30/2026. The 10Y fell 36.4 bps in October after rising 53.5 bps in September.
The DXY is 101.9 (+0.42% in October). The S&P 500 is 7,580, the VIX 20.36 (+13.95% in October), and the Nasdaq Composite 25,437 (-5.30% in October).
Energy leads commodities. The Bloomberg Energy subindex gained 7.93% in October, WTI rose 15.15% and trades at 104.12. Platinum fell 16.12% and palladium 18.91% in October.

The authors compare the 2020s to the 1970s and 2000s bull-market decades. Gold gained 73% in the 2020s first half versus 452% in the 1970s and 52% in the 2000s. The second half of the 2020s is shown as unknown.
The IGWT Gold Price Model gives a probability-weighted 2030 peak of USD 4,821.78 in the base case and USD 8,926 in the inflationary scenario.

Shadow gold price at 25% backing of M0 is USD 6,624, at 40% it is USD 10,598, and at 100% it is USD 26,494. US gold reserves at the 1980 ratio to public debt imply USD 31,312 per ounce, against 3,875 now.

The authors' 'New 60/40' portfolio is 45% stocks, 15% bonds, 15% safe-haven gold, 10% performance gold (silver and miners), 10% commodities and 5% bitcoin. The optimal gold allocation for Sharpe maximisation is 14-18%.
Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold is 0.52. Gold market cap is about USD 27.4tn against bitcoin at about USD 1.55tn.
The Incrementum Active Aurum Signal and Inflation Signal charts are included, but the text does not state the current signal reading.

sector_views.rationale: The report shows miners falling more than bullion in September and October 2026 (GDX -12.2% in October versus gold -6.8%) and gives no explicit view on the sector.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Headline inflation re-accelerated from 3.40% in August after peaking at 4.25% in May 2026.
Core inflation is well below headline, which leaves energy as the likely driver.
Producer prices are rising at the fastest pace in the two-year table.
Imported inflation is accelerating, from 6.74% in August.
The fed funds futures chart is shown from this starting point, but the report gives no text on the implied path.
The 10Y fell 36.4 bps in October after rising 53.5 bps in September.
The model's probability-weighted peak for 2030 is USD 4,821.78. The inflationary scenario gives USD 8,926.

crypto_views: Bitcoin's 90-day correlation with gold is 0.52 and its 15-day correlation is 0.69.
Bitcoin's market cap is about USD 1,552bn against gold at USD 27,395bn. The report points to the Incrementum Bitcoin Compass for more on bitcoin.
Bitcoin is 5% of the authors' 'New 60/40' portfolio.
risk_factors: Gold has fallen in 3 of the last 4 months, with -6.57% in September and -6.76% in October.
Silver is down 31.1% YTD in USD, and miners are down 10-17% in October.
The 2000s analogue shows gold's second half of the decade gaining 150%, while the 2020s second half is still unknown. The authors do not state which path they expect.
